title: Abiding in Christ
definition: Abiding in Christ is the believer's continual dependence, fellowship, obedience, and fruitfulness in union with Jesus.
summary: Abiding in Christ is the believer's daily dependence on Jesus as the source of life, obedience, communion, and fruit.
christFocus: Jesus Christ is the true vine, and His disciples bear fruit only as they abide in Him.

studySections.heading: Doctrine in Summary
studySections.content:
Abiding in Christ is the believer's ongoing dependence on Jesus for life, communion, obedience, and fruitfulness. Scripture uses the picture of branches remaining in the vine to show that disciples cannot produce spiritual life apart from Christ.

Abiding is not passive drifting. It includes receiving Christ's Word, obeying His commands, praying, trusting, and staying near Him when life is ordinary, painful, or busy.

Jesus is the true vine. The Christian life is not sustained by self-effort but by living fellowship with Him.

studySections.heading: Why This Matters
studySections.content: Believers often try to live for Christ while functionally depending on themselves. Abiding corrects performance-driven discipleship and comforts weak believers by showing that fruit comes from remaining in Christ.

studySections.heading: Discipleship and Application
studySections.content: Begin ordinary days by turning your heart to Christ, His Word, and prayer. Ask where you are striving apart from Him, and measure fruitfulness first by faithful dependence before visible results.
